- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts show excessive upward momentum after sharp price spikes; model tends to overshoot and then correct too slowly.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after peaks.
- Forecast bias is strongest in the middle-to-late horizon (days 15–30), where model remains too high relative to true values.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing downward trends; true price drops often occur before model adjusts.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short-term (1–5 days) and overly pessimistic in the long-term (25–30 days) — suggests horizon-specific calibration issues.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or cyclical patterns in the 30-day window, leading to persistent overestimation in the latter half.
